newsitem.title: USA: Barshefsky says progress slow on China WTO entry.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky says progress slow on China WTO entry.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Thursday that progress in China's bid to join the World Trade Organization was slow.

She told the Women's National Democratic Club that the United States was "not looking for a political fix" and that China's entry to the world trading forum would have to be on a "commercially meaningful" basis and result in more open markets.
"There is no other way," Barshefsky said. U.S. and Chinese trade officials met this week to discuss Beijing's bid to join the WTO.
Barshefsky met Wednesday with China's Vice Trade Minister Long Yongtu on Wednesday to discuss the WTO and the roadmap of reforms U.S. officials have told Beijing are needed to join the WTO.

"We went through a large portion of the roadmap and indicated to the Chinese that we do expect to receive full responses to the issues which are there," Barshefsky said of the talks with Chinese officials.
Barshefsky said in her luncheon speech that although China has made significant progress in opening its markets, there was still a long way to go.
"Progress for their accession is slow because we are not looking for a political fix here; we're looking for market access," Barshefsky said.
She also told the group that if President Clinton were re-elected in November, access to foreign markets would continue to be a key focus of U.S. trade policy.
